question.leadin: This conflict began due to a dispute over whether Native Americans should be driven out of Virginia.
question.text: Name this 1676 rebellion against colonial governor William Berkeley. It collapsed after its namesake died of dysentery.
question.clue: AnnCotton described this event in a letter titled "An account of our late troubles in" the colony whereit tookplace.

swap.leadin: Give the following about Spanish Florida.
swap.text: The Spanish founded this city in Florida in 1565, making it America's oldest city.
swap.clue: The 1763 Treaty of Paris ceded this city's colony, against which James Oglethorpe led a 1740 expedition.

question.text: This man founded Rhode Island after being banished from the Massachusetts Bay Colony for arguing for the separation of church and state.
question.clue: Earlier in his life, he chafed at Archbishop William Laud's strict control of Anglican Church doctrine, escaping with his wife Mary to Boston.

swap.leadin: This publication predicted the death of Titan Leeds in 1732. Leeds wasn't dead in 1733, but this publication printed an obituary anyway; when Leeds protested, this publication suspected an imposter.
swap.text: Name this annual publication, filled with astronomical information, poems, proverbs, and a calendar, that was extremely popular in the American colonies.
swap.clue: Naval hero John Paul Jones named his ship after this publication.

question.text: Ivar the Boneless conquered this city, which then became the center of the Danelaw. This city was the birthplace of the scholar Alcuin, who was the head of the palace school at Aachen.
question.clue: A scholar born in this city devised the first Western European script with lower-case letters and spacing between words and headed the palace school at Aachen.

swap.leadin: It was built by Contrecoeur in 1754 to secure the Ohio Valley during the French and Indian War.
swap.text: Name this French fort in Pennsylvania which was the target of the Braddock expedition, which turned into a fiasco. Fort Necessity was built to increase British power in the region so that an attack on this fort could occur.
swap.clue: This place was part of a series of fortifications including Fort Machault and Fort Le Boeuf.

question.text: In North America, the Seven Years' War actually lasted nine years and was known by this name, referring to Britain's two major opponents. It helped fuel the colonial grievances which later led to the American Revolution.
question.clue: A namesake expedition in this conflict was ambushed at the Monongahela River by forces under Daniel Beaujeu, leading to the death of General Braddock.

swap.leadin: This time period was aggravated by the crashing of the Sea Venture in Bermuda and the loss of effective leadership when John Smith departed.
swap.text: Name this season which only sixty people survived in the affected area. It ended when Thomas West, Baron De la Warr brought ships full of supplies and John Rolfe introduced tobacco planting.
swap.answerHtml: the “starving time” [or the winter from 1609 to 1610; or the winter from 1609 to 1610; prompt “1609;” prompt “1610”]
swap.clue: A major cause of this period, during which some relief came from trade with the Nansemonds, was the failure of the Third Supply due to the wreck of the Sea Venture, an event which inspired The Tempest.

question.leadin: This man was stabbed to death in 1769 by a member of the Peoria tribe.
question.text: Name this chief of the Ottawa tribe and victor at the Battle of Bloody Run. Fort Pitt was besieged during a war named for this man.
question.clue: A reward for this man's death was announced by Jeffrey Amherst.

swap.leadin: Its first assembly was presided over by George Yeardley, who had earlier participated in the ill-fated Third Supply Mission.
swap.text: Name this legislative body, the first such body in the British Colonies. White landowning men over 17 had the right to vote in members, and in 1699 it was moved to Williamsburg.
swap.clue: Distinguished members included Captain Francis West and Reverend William Wickham.

question.leadin: This phrase first appeared in the Pennsylvania Gazette.
question.text: Name this three word phrase which appears in a 1754 political cartoon designed by Ben Franklin, which featured a snake representing the American colonies cut into eighths. Franklin's use of the phrase was intended to promote the unity of the colonies.
question.clue: To compel Americans to get involved in the Revolution, Ben Franklin created a political cartoon with a snake divided into parts bearing the names of the colonies with this three-word phrase appearing at the bottom.

swap.leadin: This man founded Fort Christina and was the first governor of New Sweden.
swap.text: Name this Dutchman who had earlier purchased the island of Manhattan from Native Americans for goods worth sixty guilders, or twenty-four dollars.
swap.clue: This non-Swede's unintentional support of patroons who participated in the illegal fur trade led to the Dutch West India Company relieving him of his post.

question.leadin: This administrator established a council called the Nine Men to assist with governance.
question.text: Name this administrator who ignored the Flushing Remonstrance protesting his torture of preacher Robert Hodgson. The Peach War occurred during the tenure of this final director-general of New Netherland.
question.clue: He was also plagued by poor Indian relations, as shown by the outbreak of the Peach Tree War and conflicts near the village of Esopus, which he renamed Wildwyck.

swap.text: This is the Governor of New York who Zenger criticized for seizing Indian lands and rigging the 1734 elections. He died of TB approximately one year after the Zenger trial.
swap.clue: This man convened a chancery court to sue his predecessor, Rip Van Dam, whom he accused of appropriating part of his salary.

question.leadin: Give some answers about a colony that didn't make it into the original thirteen United States.
question.text: This innovation of Reverend Solomon Stoddard created a tier of church membership whose requirements were less onerous for less pious descendants of the original New England settlers.
question.clue: This relaxation of church policy in colonial New England which allowed second and third generation settlers to gain partial membership.

swap.leadin: Thomas Morton gave this man the nickname "Captain Shrimp."
swap.text: Name this leader of the Plymouth Colony militia. His unsuccessful wooing of Priscilla Mullens was fictionalized in a Henry Wadsworth Longfellow poem titled for his "courtship."
swap.clue: This military officer sailed on the Mayflower to Plymouth Colony, where he led expeditions to break up a colony at Merry Mount. There isn't any evidence that he was in a love triangle with John Alden and Priscilla Mullins.

question.leadin: Name these things about James Oglethorpe's role in the War of Jenkins' Ear.
question.text: At this skirmish on St. Simons Island, Oglethorpe caused a Spanish retreat that set up his defensive stand at Bloody Marsh.

swap.leadin: He was described as the "torchbearer of the revolution" in a book by Thomas Jefferson Wertenbacker, but that positive interpretation of his major action was opposed in a 1957 book by Wilcomb Washburn.
swap.text: Name this revolutionary leader, who defended his actions in a "Declaration of the People" issued at Middle Plantation.
swap.clue: This man called an Assembly to stamp out corruption and raise tobacco prices.

question.leadin: This conflict was sparked when its namesake was attacked on his ferry on the Susquehanna and was forced to defend himself with oars.
question.text: Name this colonial conflict of the 1730s, fought over conflicting property disputes in the Susquehanna- Codorus Creek region, which mostly consisted of border raids.

swap.text: Michael Pauw founded this settlement in New Netherland, which later grew into the cities of Hoboken and Jersey City. In 1643, Willem Kieft ordered a massacre of the Lenape at this location which prompted a furious response that almost destroyed New Amsterdam.
